title: Wrong VLAN Assignment
symptome: PC1 cannot reach its default gateway
expected-fault: Wrong VLAN assignment
expected_fix: Assign SW1 Fa0/1 to VLAN 10

title: Trunk Disabled
symptome: PC1 cannot reach its default gateway
expected-fault: Trunk not configured on Switch0 Fa0/4
expected_fix: Configure Switch0 Fa0/4 as a trunk

title: VLAN 30 Missing
symptome: Device on Fa0/3 cannot communicate with the VLAN 30 gateway
expected-fault: VLAN 30 has been deleted from Switch0
expected_fix: Recreate VLAN 30 and assign Fa0/3 to VLAN 30

title: VLAN 30 Not Allowed on Trunk
symptome: Device on Fa0/3 cannot communicate with the VLAN 30 gateway
expected-fault: VLAN 30 is not allowed on Switch0 Fa0/4 trunk
expected_fix: Allow VLAN 30 on Switch0 Fa0/4 trunk

title: Access Port in Trunk Mode
symptome: Device on Fa0/3 cannot communicate correctly with VLAN 30
expected-fault: Switch0 Fa0/3 is incorrectly configured as a trunk
expected_fix: Configure Fa0/3 as an access port and assign it to VLAN 30

title: VLAN 30 Router Subinterface Shutdown
symptome: Device in VLAN 30 cannot communicate with its default gateway
expected-fault: VLAN 30 router subinterface G0/0/0.30 is administratively down
expected_fix: Enable Router0 G0/0/0.30 with no shutdown

title: Wrong IP Address on VLAN 30 Gateway
symptome: Device in VLAN 30 cannot communicate with its expected default gateway
expected-fault: Wrong IP address configured on Router0 G0/0/0.30
expected_fix: Change G0/0/0.30 IP address back to 192.168.30.1

title: Wrong PC Default Gateway
symptome: PC can reach local gateway but cannot communicate with remote VLAN
expected-fault: PC default gateway is incorrectly configured as 192.168.20.254
expected_fix: Change PC default gateway to 192.168.20.1

title: ACL Blocking Specific Host
symptome: PC 192.168.20.10 can reach its gateway 192.168.20.1 but cannot reach 192.168.30.10
expected-fault: ACL blocks traffic from source host 192.168.20.10 to destination host 192.168.30.10
expected_fix: Configure ACL 101 to deny 192.168.20.10 to 192.168.30.10 and permit all other IP traffic

title: Router VLAN 10 Subinterface Shutdown
symptome: PC in VLAN 10 cannot reach its default gateway 192.168.10.1
expected-fault: GigabitEthernet0/0/0.10 is administratively down because shutdown is configured
expected_fix: Enter interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0.10 and use no shutdown

title: NAT Inside/Outside Misconfiguration
symptome: Static NAT mapping exists for 192.168.20.10 to 192.168.30.100 but NAT interface roles are incorrectly configured
expected-fault: G0/0/0.20 is incorrectly configured as NAT outside instead of NAT inside
expected_fix: Configure G0/0/0.20 with no ip nat outside followed by ip nat inside and keep G0/0/0.30 as ip nat outside

title: DHCP Wrong Network Configuration
symptome: VLAN 30 PC cannot obtain a valid DHCP address and shows 0.0.0.0
expected-fault: DHCP pool is configured for 192.168.40.0/24 instead of the actual VLAN 30 network 192.168.30.0/24
expected_fix: Change the DHCP pool network to 192.168.30.0 255.255.255.0 and default gateway to 192.168.30.1

title: Correct VLAN Assignment - Reference Case
symptome: PC1 can communicate through the correctly assigned VLAN
expected-fault: No fault - correct VLAN assignment
expected_fix: No fix required - VLAN assignment is correct

title: Correct Trunk Configuration - Reference Case
symptome: Trunk link is operational and required VLANs are allowed
expected-fault: No fault - correct 802.1Q trunk configuration
expected_fix: No fix required - trunk configuration is correct

title: DHCP Scope Mismatch
symptome: PC0 and PC1 get incorrect DHCP addresses
expected-fault: DHCP pool network statement does not match the intended LAN network
expected_fix: Reconfigure the DHCP pool network to 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0 or correct the router interface network

title: Incorrect DHCP DNS Server IP
symptome: PC0 can ping the DNS server IP directly but DNS name resolution fails
expected-fault: DHCP pool distributes an incorrect DNS server address
expected_fix: Change dns-server to 192.168.10.50 under the DHCP pool

title: Router LAN Interface Administratively Down
symptome: PC0 and PC1 lose connectivity to the gateway
expected-fault: GigabitEthernet0/0/0 has been administratively shut down
expected_fix: Enter interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0 and issue no shutdown

title: Inactive DNS Service
symptome: PC0 can ping the DNS server but DNS name resolution fails
expected-fault: DNS service is disabled on Server0
expected_fix: Enable the DNS service on Server0

title: Wireless Security Key Mismatch
symptome: Laptop0 is unable to connect to the wireless network
expected-fault: WPA2-PSK passphrase on Laptop0 does not match the access point
expected_fix: Update Laptop0 WPA2-PSK passphrase to match the AP

title: Missing Access Control List for Guest
symptome: Guest Wi-Fi clients can access the internal network
expected-fault: Inbound guest-isolation ACL is missing
expected_fix: Apply an extended ACL blocking the guest subnet 192.168.20.0/24 from accessing the internal subnet 192.168.10.0/24 on the guest interface

title: Guest Access Control List Enforced
symptome: Guest Wi-Fi clients cannot access the internal network
expected-fault: Inbound extended ACL correctly blocks guest access to the internal network
expected_fix: No fix required; ACL is operating as intended

title: Wireless Sticky Client Roaming Failure Due to High AP Power
symptome: Laptop0 retains connection to a distant access point instead of roaming to the closer AP
expected-fault: Access point transmit power or coverage range is too high causing sticky-client behavior
expected_next_command: check link metrics in PC Wireless
expected_fix: Reduce AP coverage or transmit power so the client can reassociate with the closer AP

title: Static NAT Port Forwarding Success
symptome: None; normal operation
expected-fault: None; Static NAT port forwarding is operating correctly
expected_fix: No fix required; system is operating as intended

title: Static NAT Port Forwarding Failure
symptome: Laptop0 gets Request Timeout when accessing the forwarded service
expected-fault: Server0 IP address does not match the IP configured in the static NAT mapping
expected_fix: Set Server0 IP configuration to the address expected by the static NAT mapping

title: Outbound Upstream DNS Port 53 Blocked
symptome: Laptop0 gets a DNS timeout when resolving external names
expected-fault: Router0 ACL blocks outbound DNS traffic on UDP/TCP port 53
expected_fix: Add an ACL permit rule on Router0 allowing DNS traffic to the required DNS server on port 53

title: Rogue DHCP Server Disruption
symptome: Laptop0 receives an invalid DHCP address such as 192.168.0.5
expected-fault: Unauthorized DHCP server responds to DHCP requests before the legitimate DHCP server
expected_fix: Enable DHCP snooping

title: Incompatible Wireless Frequency Band
symptome: Legacy wireless printer cannot detect or connect to the wireless network
expected-fault: Wireless router is configured for a frequency band unsupported by the legacy device
expected_next_command: Inspect Wireless Router GUI > Basic Wireless Settings
expected_fix: Enable the 2.4 GHz wireless band and connect the legacy device to the 2.4 GHz SSID

title: Multi-Host Distributed DHCP IP Address Exhaustion
symptome: Legitimate PC receives an APIPA address because the DHCP pool is exhausted
expected-fault: Corporate DHCP pool has reached its maximum number of allocated addresses
expected_fix: Increase the DHCP pool maximum users and renew the client DHCP lease

title: Destination NAT Port Forwarding Reference
symptome: None; active validation required
expected-fault: None; standard destination NAT deployment reference
expected_fix: No fix required if the configured destination NAT translation is correct

title: Correct VLAN 30 Configuration
symptome: Server connected to Fa0/3 can communicate using VLAN 30
expected-fault: No fault - VLAN 30 exists and Fa0/3 is correctly assigned
expected_fix: No fix required - VLAN 30 configuration is correct
